solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former chaps in the ranks brought together by padre?

parts.note: former means bygone, in the past
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Ex-servicemen being reunited by their old army chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a military chaplain, and more loosely any clergyman with a flock to tend.

clue.text: Non-believer's article squashed by wonderful man of God?

indicators.note: the article is squashed by the wonderful piece, pressed inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
the is the definite article
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A sceptic's essay crushed by a marvellous holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like the A, but A comes from A1; the article is THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies the existence of any god is a non-believer.

clue.text: Hairy stuff not entirely distressing

indicators.note: not entirely tells us only part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Hair that is a little upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock or long strand of hair is hairy stuff, playfully put.

clue.text: One mythical bird and another decapitated, old style

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: another of the same bird, the roc

explanation.surface: Two legendary birds, one beheaded, in an antique fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate eighteenth-century decoration, full of scrolls and shells, is an artistic style.

clue.text: Somehow extract two months of the year

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December
Oct is the short form of October

explanation.surface: Pull out December and October from the calendar in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' belongs to the definition: to decoct is one particular way of extracting, by boiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Decocting draws out the essence of a substance by boiling it, a specific method of extraction.

clue.text: Explosive made tiny to go off

indicators.note: to go off suggests the letters blow apart and land rearranged

explanation.surface: A small charge built to detonate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitroglycerine-based blasting material is a high explosive.

clue.text: Drovers maybe pitching tent with camel

indicators.note: pitching throws the letters about, tossing them into new order

explanation.surface: Herders setting up camp beside a camel.
explanation.definitionFit: Drovers drive livestock to market, so they are an example of men who tend herds.

clue.text: Copper on bike getting Young Conservative taken off into cell

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: taken off means these letters are removed from the bike

parts.note: a bicycle is a bike
YC stands for Young Conservative, a member of the Tory youth wing

explanation.surface: A policeman on a bicycle hauling a young Tory off to the lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small partitioned compartment, such as a shower booth, is a cell.

clue.text: Ground sterile and firm mostly — use this for better crops

indicators.note: ground as in crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: Barren, hard soil needs something to improve its harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure or chemical nutrients spread on fields help crops grow better.

clue.text: Craftily the FBI conceals senior law officer

indicators.note: done craftily, the letters of the FBI phrase are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: The American bureau is sneakily hiding a high-ranking policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a British police force holds this title, the most senior officer in the county.

clue.text: Cold joints constituting fatty food?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: Chilled cuts of meat making up a greasy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' tempts as roasts of meat; here it is the body's hinges.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-fried potato strips are a classic greasy dish, the British name for fries.

clue.text: Family identification as a comfort when things go wrong

indicators.note: things going wrong puts the letters out of order

explanation.surface: A family crest offered as consolation in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic shield design marks out a family or lineage, identifying it.

clue.text: Policeman within the law grabbing male guiltily involved?

indicators.note: the policeman grabbing the male holds that letter inside himself

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: A lawful officer arresting a man yet himself implicated in the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Being an accomplice to wrongdoing, sharing the guilt of it, is exactly this condition.

clue.text: To provide evidence is an ordeal, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: Giving testimony in court is a gruelling experience, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness or certify formally is to give evidence of something's truth.

clue.text: These will miss the direction indicated

definitions.text: These will miss the direction indicated

parts.words: These will miss the direction indicated
parts.note: the word These losing the letters of 'the' leaves two letters that abbreviate a compass point

explanation.surface: These people will fail to follow the directions given.
explanation.walkthrough: Take THE out of THESE and SE remains: that abbreviation is the compass direction it indicates.
explanation.definitionFit: SE is the standard abbreviation of the compass point between two of the four cardinal directions.

clue.text: Potential biological research material may have a strange smell etc

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, reordered into something new

explanation.surface: Lab samples might give off an odd whiff, among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Undifferentiated cells able to become many tissue types are a major focus of medical research.

clue.text: One yelling outside publishing house is dealer taking people's money

indicators.note: the yeller goes outside, wrapping round the publisher

parts.note: a crier yells, like a town crier
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A shouting man outside a publisher's turns out to be a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino employee running a gaming table collects and pays out players' stakes.

clue.text: Writing in paper, old piece, something coming after Jan

parts.note: a bit is a piece
the letters that follow Jan in the name of the first month

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about some ancient item that turns up after January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jan' looks like a person or the month's short form; the trick is the rest of the word January.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's death notice and life story of someone recently deceased is a piece of writing in a paper.

clue.text: Trim men seem to conceal what's very big

indicators.note: the phrase is said to conceal the answer within its words

explanation.surface: Slim men seem to hide something huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous or vast is very big.

clue.text: Pithy sayings conveying no message when unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping the phrase reveals what lies inside its words

explanation.surface: Short proverbs that say nothing at all once you open them up.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the garden ornaments nor Swiss bankers: these are maxims, the source of gnomic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is an aphorism or maxim, a short saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: The boss? You may see a scolding type in this person, right?

indicators.note: in places the scolding type inside this person

parts.note: this person is the speaker, me
a nag scolds persistently

explanation.surface: Might your boss be a nagging sort, don't you agree?
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of staff or a business is the boss.

clue.text: Make good fighting force, company having risen?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
having risen means being up

explanation.surface: Recover a military unit when its company has climbed back up.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to recover or compensate for them, making them good.

clue.text: Sort of accommodation in which an insect keeps maiden quiet!

indicators.note: the insect keeps the two pieces held within itself

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A lodging where a bug silences a young girl, exclamation and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable house for the poor or elderly, built by benefactors, is a form of housing.

clue.text: Fellow with gold in imposing residence

parts.note: a fellow is a man
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rich chap living in a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord's large country house with its estate is a stately home.

clue.text: A little while needed to get the answer? That can bring grumbles

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a little while
ans is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Waiting a while for a reply is enough to cause complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints and whinges are grumbles, plural nouns both.

clue.text: Fellow brave when consuming port and Eastern fruit

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the brave word consuming the port takes it inside

parts.note: daring means brave
Oran is a port in Algeria

explanation.surface: A bold man munching through a citrus from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned citrus, a tangerine type, is a fruit.

clue.text: Glower maybe as loveless type full of energy

indicators.note: the loveless type is full of energy, holding it within

parts.note: a hater is someone who loves nothing
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A scowl from a bitter, unloving person bursting with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as a scowl; it is something that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator or fire glows when switched on, so it is a thing that glows.

clue.text: The old man's attempt to get food from the bakery

parts.note: pa is father, the old man, and the possessive gives an S
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at fetching something from the baker's.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked dough goods such as tarts and pies are sold at a bakery.
